style: A city wall of wheatpasted posters: Anton at billboard size over Work Sans small print, fluoro yellow, pink, cobalt and orange paper on grey concrete, posters that paste up and settle, a 48-sheet billboard and a tear-off flyer for contact.

concept.idea: Ads used to be pasted up on walls, and the good ones still work like posters: one line, read in a second, loud enough to stop someone. The site is a wall of the agency's own posters: the specialties are flyposters, the services a four-poster series, the audience a billboard and the contact a tear-off flyer.
concept.signature: The hero goes up like a wheatpaste: the big tagline poster and then six channel posters are brushed on from the top one after another, each landing at its own slight angle, and one corner keeps peeling at rest. Every poster below settles flat against the wall as it reaches the screen. All posters fully pasted without JS or with reduced motion.

jury.note: Self-score from the /jury rubric and shoot.mjs evidence (0 axe violations, no horizontal overflow at 390 or 1440 with sample and long.json, no tap target under 24 px, every focus stop visible, skip link first, nothing moving under reduced motion). No blind critic was run for this batch. Loud and specific: posters paste up and settle, one corner peels at rest, the audience is a billboard and contact is a tear-off flyer. Angled posters and all-caps Anton cost a little reading speed, so design and usability are held at 7.5.
